text:
john_support: FYI customer ACME reported their service endpoint svc.acme.prod.internal started failing with TLS cert mismatch and intermittent NXDOMAINs this morning. They see public IPs in some regions. Ticket #4321.
john_support: Repro steps they gave:
```
# from their prod VPC
dig +short svc.acme.prod.internal @10.0.0.2
# sometimes returns 3.35.22.11 (public), sometimes NXDOMAIN
curl -v https://svc.acme.prod.internal --resolve 'svc.acme.prod.internal:443:3.35.22.11'
# TLS error: server certificate is for example.com
```
john_support: Attached the traceroute and cURL output. Customer says this started after a Hosted Zone merge last night. Can eng look? :eyes:
alice_sre: I pulled a quick dig from our vantage in us-west-2:
```
dig +short svc.acme.prod.internal @10.0.1.2
# -> 10.2.5.12
dig +short svc.acme.prod.internal @resolver-01.acme.vpc
# -> 3.35.22.11
```
alice_sre: Looks like split-horizon: some resolvers returning private record, some returning public Route53 record.
maya_prodeng: Confirming - I see two private hosted zones for acme: hz-aaaa (vpc assoc: vpc-1111) and hz-bbbb (vpc assoc: vpc-2222) — both have an A for svc.acme.prod.internal but different answers. One was created during last-night migration.
maya_prodeng: route53 list-hosted-zones-by-name output: 
```
Name: svc.acme.prod.internal.  ID: /hostedzone/HZAAAA  Private: true
Name: svc.acme.prod.internal.  ID: /hostedzone/HZBBBB  Private: true
```
maya_prodeng: Also seeing resolver-rule overlap for the tenant account that routes .prod.internal to a forwarder in multiple VPCs. That could send queries to the wrong private zone depending on resolver path.
dns_bot: (automated check) Ran VPC association consistency check for account acme-prod:
- hz-aaaa associated with vpc-1111 (us-west-2)
- hz-bbbb associated with vpc-2222 (us-east-1)
- overlapping name detected: svc.acme.prod.internal
"split-horizon-risk": true
dns_bot: Suggests recommended_action: consolidate/remove duplicate private hosted zone or ensure VPC associations are scoped correctly.
john_support: Customer says they added the new hosted zone during the merge to redirect traffic to egress ALB in us-east-1. They didn't expect it to affect us-west callers.
alice_sre: Two possible causes: resolver rule/forwarder routing queries to the us-east VPC (giving public egress IP) or Route53 private-hosted-zone misassociations where the us-west resolver can't see the correct zone and falls back to public record.
tim_oncall: Any recent infra deploys that touch resolver/forwarder?
deploybot: Deploys last 24h: resolver-forwarder v2.1.3 rolled to us-east-1 at 03:12, us-west-2 at 03:25. No config changes recorded for forwarder route priorities.
tim_oncall: Ok. Next steps: 1) repro from within affected VPCs, 2) capture dig +trace and tcpdump on resolver path, 3) inspect Route53 VPC associations and resolver rules priorities.
maya_prodeng: I'm running the recommended repro from within the customer's vpc-1111 (us-west-2):
```
# on an ec2 in vpc-1111
dig +trace +short svc.acme.prod.internal
dig +short @10.0.1.2 svc.acme.prod.internal
# got 10.2.5.12 locally, but when I query resolver's forwarder 10.0.0.5 -> returns 3.35.22.11
```
maya_prodeng: tcpdump on 10.0.1.2 shows queries forwarded to 10.0.0.5 in some flows. That forwarder is in the us-east VPC and resolves to the other private zone.
alice_sre: That explains intermittent behaviour depending on which resolver path the client picks.
john_support: Customer also reported TLS cert mismatch when reaching 3.35.22.11 — cert is for their external ALB (example.com), not internal svc cert. So requests get bounced by our mutual TLS checks.
maya_prodeng: Short-term mitigation: update resolver rule priority so vpc-1111 resolves locally first (no forwarding) OR temporarily remove the us-east private hosted zone association from the shared resolver VPC to prevent leakage.
tim_oncall: We should verify impact before removing associations. I'll open a rapid change with read-only removal in staging first.
alice_sre: Policy note: we can't delete the zone without CS approval; do we have ACME CSE signoff for rollbacks?
john_support: I've pinged CSM @carlos to approve an emergency rollback for the hosted-zone merge. Waiting on reply. :phone:
maya_prodeng: Longer-term: prevent duplicate private-hosted-zone names across tenant accounts or enforce unique naming with zone IDs during merges. Add a pre-merge guard in the merge script to detect overlapping private zones and fail.
dns_bot: I've created an incident checklist entry: "split-horizon private-hosted-zone overlap" with repro steps and rollback playbook. Incident ID: INC-2026-089.
deploybot: Rolling a quick resolver-rule priority change to staging cluster in us-west-2 now.
# short pause
deploybot: staging change successful. Can someone validate dig results from staging VPC?
maya_prodeng: Validated in staging: queries now consistently return local private IP 10.2.5.12. TLS handshake succeeds against internal cert.
john_support: Marking customer ticket as "mitigated - routing change applied to staging; awaiting prod CSM approval for removal of conflicting hosted zone association". Will update ACME.
alice_sre: Note for postmortem: include root cause (hosted zone duplication + resolver rule overlap) and action items: rollback guard, pre-merge automated check, alerting on private-hosted-zone name collisions.
tim_oncall: I'll schedule a follow-up incident review tomorrow. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
john_support: Thanks team — I'll keep the ticket open until ACME confirms full resolution.
